pattern.top_pattern: CO specialty facility mix is spiking in Children's and unmapped claims
pattern.what_is_impacting: CO Commercial Individual HMO Children's and unmapped facility claims
pattern.pattern_details: Outside the core CO acute-hospital surge, there is a separate mix shift into Children's settings and claims without a mapped facility. Both areas show more admissions and higher paid per admit, which suggests a combination of real site-of-care pressure and classification risk. This needs a split response: validate the unmapped claims first, then address pediatric or specialty site economics directly.
pattern.why_it_matters: This pattern blends true specialty-facility cost pressure with possible facility mapping leakage, so business action has to separate the two.
pattern.recommended_next_step: First correct facility mapping for the unmapped CO claims, then run a targeted Children's site-of-care and reimbursement review for HMO inpatient admissions.
pattern.validation_reason: Part of the increase sits in unmapped facility claims, so facility attribution should be confirmed before contracting or UM action is expanded.
evidence_summary: CO HMO Children's claims added about +$7.7M on 82 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $94K.
CO HMO not-mapped facility claims added about +$6.0M on 110 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $26K.
Both pockets sit outside the main CO acute-hospital utilization story, pointing to site mix or facility classification issues rather than only broad inpatient demand.
